text: dsh-speak 是面向 DSH 网页客户端的语音朗读插件，通过注册 speak 工具和网页控件，调用运行 DSH 的 macOS 机器上的 say 命令朗读文本。它支持助手朗读或停止、逐条助手回复朗读、选中文本朗读，以及按语言选择声音、调节语速和设置无假名汉字的语言偏好。适合希望免用外部语音服务，在 DSH 中听取回复或选中文本的用户；需要 macOS。

dsh-speak adds a speak tool and web controls for reading DSH text aloud with macOS say. It can read assistant replies or selected page text, stop playback, and configure voices by language, rate, and Han text bias. Requires macOS.

dsh-speak 的功能「助手语音朗读」：speak 工具接收文本，清理 Markdown 后按文字脚本分段，并用 macOS say 依次朗读；可传语言、声音、语速选项，也可停止当前播放。
dsh-speak 的功能「朗读助手回复」：每条已完成的助手回复下方提供扬声器操作，点击即可朗读该条回复，再次点击可停止；新的朗读会替换当前播放。
dsh-speak 的功能「选区朗读」：在网页选择非输入控件中的文本后显示朗读气泡，点击即可让主机朗读选中文字，并可从同一气泡停止。
dsh-speak 的功能「语音设置」：设置面板可按中文、英语、日语、韩语选择已安装声音，调节语速并设定无假名汉字的语言偏好；设置保存至 DSH_HOME 下的文件。
dsh-speak 使用 macOS say 命令进行本机语音播放，因此运行 DSH 的环境需要 macOS；配置设置保存在 DSH_HOME 下。见 index.js:32、index.js:522。
想用快捷键快速停止正在播放的朗读。

dsh-speak README · dsh-speak：Read text aloud in the [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH), on the machine running it, with the macOS `say` command.

**English** | [中文](README.zh.md)

dsh-speak README · dsh-speak：| Entry | Where | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `speak` tool | the model can call it | reads text aloud, or stops with `stop: true` |
| 🔊 message action | the action strip under every finalized assistant reply | click to read that reply, click again to **stop** |
| 🔊 select-to-read bubble | above any text you select on the page | "select and read", like select-to-translate |
| ⚙ reading settings | speaker-gear button in the composer dock | per-language voice, rate, and Han-character bias |

dsh-speak README · dsh-speak：Chinese, English, Japanese, and Korean are detected per character, and **every script run is read by its own system voice** in its own `say` process. One reading plays at a time; a new request replaces it.

Audio comes out of the machine running DSH, never the browser. No network calls, no API keys, no model downloads.

dsh-speak README · Requirements：- **macOS** — playback shells out to `say`. (Linux with `spd-say`, or a browser-side `speechSynthesis` variant, would be a separate provider; not implemented.)
- **DSH 0.2.x** — the desktop app, or any profile whose page is served to a browser.
- **Node 20+** only if you want to run the offline test.

dsh-speak README · A. Through the plugin manager (recommended)：1. Open DSH → **Plugins** (Settings → Plugins, or the Plugins panel in the sidebar).
2. **Install bundle** and paste the repository URL:

```
   https://github.com/RinChanNOWWW/dsh-speak
   ```

A git URL, a local absolute path, and an npm name are all accepted.
3. The bundle patch inserts one row (`speak`) and the browser half is served automatically — there is no build step and no dependencies to install.
4. Use it. If the buttons do not appear, reload the page once.

dsh-speak README · A. Through the plugin manager (recommended)：> The in-app plugin manager is the intended path for the desktop app, which is why the `dsh plugin` CLI refuses that profile. For any other profile the CLI works too — see below.

dsh-speak README · B. Manual install into a profile：Use this when you want the plugin to live outside the profile's `node_modules`.

1. Copy the package next to the profile's patch file:

```
   $DSH_HOME/profiles/<profile>/plugins/dsh-speak/{package.json,index.js,client.js}
   ```

2. Add one row to `$DSH_HOME/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
   - insert:
       - id: speak
         name: ./plugins/dsh-speak/index.js
   ```

text: dsh-speak README · B. Manual install into a profile：The `name` **must point at the entry file**: the loader resolves a `.`-prefixed name with `import(new URL(name, baseUrl))`, so a directory cannot be imported, and the browser half is found by walking up from that file to the nearest `package.json`.

dsh-speak README · B. Manual install into a profile：3. Restart the app, or let the profile reload — an **added** row is picked up live.
4. To change host code later: write a **new file** (`index.v2.js`…) and **remove then re-insert** the row. A mounted row is not re-imported when only its `name` changes, and a `?v=` query in the name is rejected by the loader. `deploy.sh` automates exactly this.

dsh-speak README · C. A `dsh web` profile：```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add https://github.com/RinChanNOWWW/dsh-speak
```

That installs the package; the bundle also has to be listed in that profile's `package.json` → `dsh.profile.bundles` for its patch to be applied. The in-app plugin manager does both steps for you.

dsh-speak README · Ask the assistant：| `speak` argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `text` | text to read; markdown is stripped; required unless `stop` is true |
| `stop` | `true` stops the current reading instead of starting one |
| `language` | `zh` / `en` / `ja` / `ko` — biases ambiguous text (bare Han characters) and acts as the voice fallback; **does not** force one voice for everything |
| `voice` | an exact macOS voice name (`Tingting`, `Kyoko`, `Yuna`, `Samantha`…); reads the whole text in that one voice |
| `rate` | words per minute, 80–500 |
| `wait` | wait for the whole reading instead of returning as soon as it starts |
dsh-speak README · Ask the assistant：It returns the character count, the languages found, the voices used, and the **per-run sequence**, e.g. `zh:Tingting -> ko:Yuna -> ja:Kyoko -> en:Samantha`.

dsh-speak README · From the interface：- **Message action** — 🔊 under a finalized reply. While it reads, the icon highlights and its sound waves pulse; click again to stop. If another reply is being read it dims (clicking switches to this one), and a failure shows red with a retry hint.
- **Select to read** — select text anywhere that is not an input; a small bubble appears above the selection (below it when there is no room, always clamped to the viewport). Click it to read; the bubble **stays and becomes "stop reading"**. Selections inside inputs, textareas, and `contenteditable` regions are ignored, as is anything over 20,000 characters.
- **Settings** — the speaker-gear button in the composer dock, or the gear inside the selection bubble.

dsh-speak README · Stopping a reading：| Way | Notes |
|---|---|
| the same bubble, now "停止朗读 / Stop reading" | it no longer dismisses itself when it starts |
| the floating **stop** pill, bottom right | appears while *anything* plays — including a reading the agent started through the tool — because the page keeps a slow status heartbeat |
| **⌘⇧S** (Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+S) | works anywhere, including inside the composer; rebindable in DSH's shortcut settings as `speak.stop` |
| ask the assistant | `speak` with `stop: true` |

dsh-speak README · Settings：The panel offers, per language (中文 / English / 日本語 / 한국어), the voices actually installed on the machine — recommended ones first — plus a rate slider, a **Bare Han** switch (whether Han characters without kana read as Chinese or Japanese), a preview button, and save state.

They are stored in `$DSH_HOME/dsh-speak.settings.json` and also drive the `speak` tool, so the assistant reads with the voices you picked. Explicit tool arguments override them for one reading.

dsh-speak README · Settings：```bash
curl -s $DSH_WEB_URL/api/dsh-speak/settings   # installed voices + current settings
```

dsh-speak README · How it works：Two halves in one package (one loader row):

- `index.js` — the host half. Registers the `speak` tool and four routes on the composition's web server:

dsh-speak README · How it works：| Route | Purpose |
  |---|---|
  | `POST /api/dsh-speak` | `{action:"speak", text?/sessionId+messageId}` or `{action:"stop"}` |
  | `GET /api/dsh-speak/status` | what is playing now: source, message identity, languages, voices, sequence, progress |
  | `GET/POST /api/dsh-speak/settings` | read/write preferences; lists installed voices |
  | `GET/POST /api/dsh-speak/client` | the browser half's report channel (see *Diagnostics*) |

dsh-speak README · How it works：- `client.js` — the browser half, a prebuilt bundle in the format the client module loader expects (`window.__ModuleLoader__.load({id, factory})`). It registers four slots: `conversation.chat.assistant-actions`, two entries in `shell.overlay`, and `conversation.composer.dock`.

Language handling:

dsh-speak README · How it works：- Kana makes a Han/kana run Japanese; Hangul is Korean; Latin is English; a kana-free Han run follows the **Bare Han** setting.
- Sentence-ending punctuation and script changes split runs, so `中文句子。日本語の文。` keeps two voices.
- Latin runs shorter than `MIN_LATIN_RUN` (12 characters of their own script, default) are folded into the surrounding language, so an acronym inside Chinese prose does not flip the voice for three words. CJK and Hangul runs are never absorbed.
- Playback is one `say` process per run, started when the previous one exits: `say` has **no inline voice switch** (its `[[...]]` commands cover rate, pitch, volume, and input mode only), and an unsupported `[[voice:…]]` is read out as literal text.

dsh-speak README · Diagnostics：The browser half reports what it loaded and did to `GET /api/dsh-speak/client` (a 200-entry ring buffer in the host): `hello` (build + registered entries), `style`, `mounted`, `visibility`, `rendered` (the measured box, whether it is inside the viewport, and which ancestor would break `position: fixed`), `error` (with the component stack), plus settings and playback transitions. That is how "I clicked and nothing appeared" gets answered without devtools.

dsh-speak README · Diagnostics：```bash
curl -s $DSH_WEB_URL/api/dsh-speak/client
```

dsh-speak README · Troubleshooting：| Symptom | Check |
|---|---|
| nothing is read | `curl -s $DSH_WEB_URL/api/dsh-speak/status` — `speaking` should be non-null; then `.../client` for a browser-side failure |
| buttons missing | reload the page; a changed `client.js` only reaches the page when the row is recomposed |
| old host code still runs | a mounted row is not re-imported on a `name` change; deploy a new filename and remove/re-insert the row (`deploy.sh`) |
| wrong voice | the settings panel: a per-language pin wins, then the recommended voice for that language, then the system default |
| bare Han read in the wrong language | set **Bare Han** to 中文 or 日文 — kana-free Han text is genuinely ambiguous |
| `unknown session` (422) | the message belongs to a session this Harness process has not loaded |

dsh-speak README · Development：```bash
pnpm install      # only for @deepseek-ai/dsh-tools, used by index.js and the test
pnpm test         # offline host-half suite; spawns the real `say`, so it makes noise
./deploy.sh       # deploy into the running profile and wait for the reload (dev helper)
```

`deploy.sh` writes a new versioned entry file, removes and re-inserts the profile row, waits for the status route to come back, and keeps one entry file. It reads `$DSH_PROFILE_DIR` and falls back to `$DSH_HOME/profiles/desktop`.

dsh-speak README · Development：The test suite stubs the tool registry, session store, and web server, and points the settings file at a temporary `DSH_HOME`, so it neither needs DSH nor touches your preferences.

dsh-speak README · Security notes：- Routes only accept `POST`/`GET` and require `application/json`, so a cross-origin page hits a CORS preflight it cannot pass, and a simple request is rejected with 415. Text never leaves the machine — it goes straight to `say`.
- The plugin deliberately does not apply DSH's connection trust fence to its routes, so they can be exercised with `curl`. It only ever makes the host speak.
